svg.title: The rail
svg.desc: A line of time from 1000 BC at the top to AD 40 at the bottom, 1.25 units a year, with every row of the anchor table on it: 41 rows, each drawn as Fixed (solid), Anchored (hollow) or Bracketed (dashed range), with its error bar to scale. 31 rows carry a year or less. Bands mark the five outside records that date each stretch: Assyria, Babylon, Persia, The Greeks, Rome. Red bars beside the line are the spans Scripture counts: Jeremiah's seventy years (605 BC to 536 BC); Seventy years of indignation (586 BC to 515 BC); Daniel's 69 weeks (444 BC to AD 33); 2,300 evenings and mornings (171 BC to 164 BC). Above the line, dashed, the Exodus in 1446 BC and creation in 3959 BC, counted back from row 1.
svg.text: Forty-one anchors from Solomon's temple to the cross, to scale
Jehu pays tribute to Shalmaneser III ±1
Malachi, the last writing prophet 460-400 BC
Alexander dies; the horn is broken ±0
Antiochus III takes Judea at Panium ±2
Onias III murdered; Menelaus high priest ±1
Temple desecrated; the abomination set up ±0
Pompey takes Jerusalem; Rome rules Judea ±0
Above the rail: the Exodus, 1446 BC, 480 years before row 1 (1 Kings 6:1)
and creation, 3959 BC, AM 0, counted back through Genesis 5 and 11
Fixed: computable, or a record naming the event
Anchored: a stated interval from a fixed point
Bracketed: held between two dated points
The spans Scripture counts, beside the line:
Jeremiah's seventy years, 605 BC to 536 BC: counted inclusively (Jeremiah 25:11-12; Daniel
Seventy years of indignation, 586 BC to 515 BC (Zechariah 1:12; 7:5)
Daniel's 69 weeks, 444 BC to AD 33: 483 years of 360 days (476 of ours) (Daniel 9:25-26;
2,300 evenings and mornings, 171 BC to 164 BC: as days, on one reading (Daniel 8:14)
Dashed: this site's reading, or contested
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
